bug_description.normalized: In the staged vulnerable revision a9c8d2a9493c4e0cd201db57801f3502e65c686c, `file_trycdf` feeds the attacker-controlled CDF document into the summary-information parser, which loads the `\05SummaryInformation` user stream into a 17-sector heap buffer. `cdf_unpack_summary_info` then reads the first section declaration from that buffer, converts `sd->sd_offset`, and passes the resulting attacker-controlled `offs` value to `cdf_read_property_info`, where the witnessed section header says `sh_len = 8260` and `sh_properties = 18`. On the crashing property iteration, `cdf_read_property_info` resolves a property record with `pi_type = 0x1f` (`CDF_LENGTH32_WSTRING`), computes `left = 8052`, reads the attacker-controlled length field `l = 253`, and verifies only that `o4 + l <= left` (`8 + 253 <= 8052`). It stores `inp[i].pi_str.s_len = l` and `inp[i].pi_str.s_buf = &q[o4]`, but the debug print at line 1092 uses `%s` instead of a precision-bounded format, so the active `DPRINTF`/`printf` call ignores `l` and scans past the property payload until it crosses the end of the 8704-byte stream allocation. AddressSanitizer reports `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 8425` in `cdf_read_property_info`; the fix changes the format to `%.*s`, bounding the print to `l` bytes.

source.description: First project-code statement on the crashing path that materializes the attacker-controlled bytes and length into `cdf_info`, the parser state later used by every `cdf_read` while building the SummaryInformation stream.
source.value_from: The libFuzzer harness in `magic_fuzzer.cc` passes the staged witness into `magic_buffer`, which reaches `file_trycdf`. The saved PoC is the exact 11264-byte CDF file `gt_results/arvo_38898/poc` (sha256 `f77e2262f7b5d4af6795d56c35ad54b64a10f8621c70bcd7ee8a2cf70d428898`); its first eight bytes are the CDF magic `d0 cf 11 e0 a1 b1 1a e1`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.code: DPRINTF(("o=%" SIZE_T_FORMAT "u l=%d(%" SIZE_T_FORMAT "u), t=%" SIZE_T_FORMAT "u s=%s\n", o4, l, CDF_ROUND(l, sizeof(l)), left, inp[i].pi_str.s_buf));
sink.description: ASan sink. The active debug print passes raw SummaryInformation property bytes to `%s`, so `printf` reads past the 253-byte payload and continues through the 8704-byte heap-backed stream buffer until it reaches the redzone.
sink.note: The saved AddressSanitizer trace reports `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 8425` at `src/cdf.c:1092`, with the faulting address 0 bytes to the right of the 8704-byte region allocated for the SummaryInformation stream.

root_cause.code: DPRINTF(("o=%" SIZE_T_FORMAT "u l=%d(%" SIZE_T_FORMAT "u), t=%" SIZE_T_FORMAT "u s=%s\n", o4, l, CDF_ROUND(l, sizeof(l)), left, inp[i].pi_str.s_buf));
root_cause.description: Root cause. In the staged vulnerable source `CDF_DEBUG` makes `DPRINTF` a live `printf` call, but this format uses `%s` instead of a precision-bounded specifier, so the declared property length `l` is ignored and the print treats `inp[i].pi_str.s_buf` as an unbounded C string. The fix changes this to `%.*s` and passes `(int)l` as the bound.
root_cause.note: The earlier `o4 + l > left` check only proves that `l` bytes exist inside the current section. It does not prove there is a NUL terminator before the end of the heap-backed stream buffer, so `%s` can walk off the allocation.

tainted_value_origin.description: The vulnerability-relevant attacker-controlled field is the length word of the current `CDF_LENGTH32_WSTRING` property. `cdf_read_property_info` reads that 32-bit size from the loaded SummaryInformation bytes and the next lines pair it with `&q[o4]`, but the later `%s` print never uses `l` to cap the read.

parser_admitted.description: By this point the witness has already passed CDF header, SAT, SSAT, directory, and short-stream parsing, and `file_trycdf` is entering the `\05SummaryInformation` user-stream path that leads to the crashing property parser.

fine_trace.note: Source. `file_trycdf` stores the attacker-controlled CDF buffer and exact length into `cdf_info`, which is the state all later `cdf_read` calls use while loading the SummaryInformation stream and its properties.

fine_trace.code: return cdf_read_sector_chain(info, h, sat, ssat, sst, d->d_stream_first_sector, d->d_size, scn);
fine_trace.note: After earlier directory parsing locates the `\05SummaryInformation` entry, `cdf_read_user_stream` forwards that entry's attacker-controlled first sector and stream size into the sector-chain loader.

fine_trace.code: scn->sst_len = cdf_count_chain(sat, sid, ss); scn->sst_dirlen = MAX(h->h_min_size_standard_stream, len); scn->sst_ss = ss;
fine_trace.note: The SummaryInformation stream's sector chain is counted and its stream geometry is derived. On the witnessed run this path yields `scn->sst_len = 17` sectors and `ss = 512`, the dimensions that later define the 8704-byte heap allocation.

Allocates the heap buffer that will hold the SummaryInformation stream. The saved run logs `cdf.c,594: cdf_calloc 17 512`, and ASan later reports the invalid read 0 bytes to the right of this 8704-byte region.

fine_trace.code: if ((nr = cdf_read_sector(info, scn->sst_tab, i * ss, ss, h, sid)) != CAST(ssize_t, ss)) {
fine_trace.note: Across the 17-iteration loop, each `cdf_read_sector` copies 512 bytes from the input-backed CDF file into `scn->sst_tab`. By loop exit, this heap buffer contains the attacker-controlled SummaryInformation stream that the later property parser walks.

fine_trace.code: const cdf_section_declaration_t *sd = CAST(const cdf_section_declaration_t *, RCAST(const void *, RCAST(const char *, sst->sst_tab) + CDF_SECTION_DECLARATION_OFFSET)); ... if (cdf_read_property_info(sst, h, CDF_TOLE4(sd->sd_offset), info, count, &maxcount) == -1)
fine_trace.note: From the loaded SummaryInformation bytes, `cdf_unpack_summary_info` reads the first section declaration at `sst->sst_tab + CDF_SECTION_DECLARATION_OFFSET` and converts its attacker-controlled `sd_offset` field into the `offs` argument passed to `cdf_read_property_info`. That `offs` value chooses which section of `sst->sst_tab` will be parsed next.

fine_trace.code: shp = CAST(const cdf_section_header_t *, cdf_offset(sst->sst_tab, offs)); ... sh.sh_len = CDF_TOLE4(shp->sh_len); ... sh.sh_properties = CDF_TOLE4(shp->sh_properties); ... p = CAST(const uint8_t *, cdf_offset(sst->sst_tab, offs + sizeof(sh))); e = CAST(const uint8_t *, cdf_offset(shp, sh.sh_len));
fine_trace.note: Using the `offs` value materialized in `cdf_unpack_summary_info`, the parser selects a section inside `sst->sst_tab` and derives its bounds. The saved run logs this section as `section len: 8260 properties 18`, so `p` becomes the property table base and `e` the end of the current section.

fine_trace.code: if ((q = cdf_get_property_info_pos(sst, h, p, e, i)) == NULL) goto out; left = CAST(size_t, e - q); inp[i].pi_type = CDF_GETUINT32(q, 0); ... nelements = 1; slen = 1; o4 = slen * sizeof(uint32_t);
fine_trace.note: For the crashing property iteration, `q` is resolved from the section's property-offset table, `left` becomes the remaining bytes in the section from that property record, and `pi_type = 0x1f` selects the `CDF_LENGTH32_WSTRING` case. Because the vector bit is clear, this path uses `nelements = 1`, `slen = 1`, and starts the string payload at `o4 = 4`.

Reads the attacker-controlled length word from the property record and advances the payload offset past that length field. In the saved run this yields `l = 253` and `o4 = 8`, matching the debug log `o=8 l=253(256), t=8052` emitted immediately before the crash.

The present bounds guard is not taken because the declared property payload fits inside the current section: `8 + 253 <= 8052`. This check only proves that `l` bytes exist from `q + o4` to `e`; it does not require a NUL terminator before the end of the 8704-byte stream allocation.

fine_trace.code: inp[i].pi_str.s_len = l; inp[i].pi_str.s_buf = CAST(const char *, CAST(const void *, &q[o4]));
fine_trace.note: Stores the declared length and a raw pointer to the property payload. `pi_str.s_buf` now aliases the current wide-string bytes inside `scn->sst_tab`, but no terminator is added and the later print will not use `pi_str.s_len` as a bound.

fine_trace.code: DPRINTF(("o=%" SIZE_T_FORMAT "u l=%d(%" SIZE_T_FORMAT "u), t=%" SIZE_T_FORMAT "u s=%s\n", o4, l, CDF_ROUND(l, sizeof(l)), left, inp[i].pi_str.s_buf));
fine_trace.note: Root cause and sink. In this vulnerable source `CDF_DEBUG` makes `DPRINTF` call `printf`, but the format uses `%s` instead of a precision-bounded `%.*s`, so the declared length `l` is ignored and the read keeps scanning from `pi_str.s_buf` until a NUL is found. On the saved run there is no terminator before the end of the 8704-byte SummaryInformation buffer, so AddressSanitizer reports `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 8425` at this line with the faulting address 0 bytes to the right of `[0x625000000100, 0x625000002300)`.

allocation_context.note: ASan reports that the invalid read crossed 0 bytes past the 8704-byte SummaryInformation buffer allocated here.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_38898 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 8425` in `cdf_read_property_info` with stack `cdf_unpack_summary_info -> cdf_check_summary_info`, matching OSS-Fuzz issue 38898.

format.name: Microsoft Composite Document File V2 (CDF) with SummaryInformation property set
format.contract: Exactly the 11264-byte witness stored in `gt_results/arvo_38898/poc` (sha256 `f77e2262f7b5d4af6795d56c35ad54b64a10f8621c70bcd7ee8a2cf70d428898`). On the saved run it is accepted as a CDF document, its `\05SummaryInformation` user stream is loaded as 17 sectors (8704 bytes), and `cdf_read_property_info()` reaches a section with `sh_len = 8260` and `sh_properties = 18`. The trigger is the current `CDF_LENGTH32_WSTRING` property record for which `left = 8052`, `o4 = 8`, and the attacker-controlled length field is `l = 253`: the property payload is not NUL-terminated before the end of the loaded stream buffer, so the vulnerable `%s` debug print at line 1092 scans past that payload and off the 8704-byte allocation.
